  "text": "By morning Tobias had worn a pale place in the brim of his hat. He sat in the last pew until the woman who swept the church asked whether he was waiting for someone.

He said he was waiting for daylight.

She looked at the windows. He did not.

Later he took the road above the dunes. There was wind now. It carried the smell of cut bait from the harbour, and somewhere a man was calling to another man about a rope. Tobias stopped where Maren's path left the road.

The eleven posts stood straight. The lantern lay beside the lowest one. Its glass was whole.

He went to the porch and knocked on the door, which was shut. After a while he tried the latch.

The front room was empty. The lamp stood unlit on the sill. He put one finger against its chimney, then withdrew it. Cold.

There was nothing to carry away. That troubled him more than he had expected. He had brought a sack, though he could not have said what he had meant to put in it.

Before leaving, he straightened the corner of her father's rug with his shoe.

At the gate he looked back. From there he could see the sill, but not the lamp. He moved a little to his left. There it was.

He stood a moment longer, fixing that place in his mind.

Then he folded the sack beneath his arm and went to tell the others that Maren was not at home.",
